Today's 17:31 scheduled system_doctor run could not execute 12 of its checks — repo clone unreadable, scheduler unreadable, live site unreachable — and reported 20🟢/30🟡/1🔴. Re-run by hand at 20:35 from the same machine, with the same paths, everything resolved: 38🟢/11🟡/2🔴. The AUTOMATED run is systematically blinder than the manual one, which is the exact failure class OFFLINE_RESILIENCE was built to kill: the health report is produced when the operator is away and is least trustworthy precisely then.

The operator's live position size and average cost shipped in the CLEARTEXT public block of the per-ticker data.json on the public Pages site. 13 names affected including all four currently-held. Emit-side stopped and the LIVE TIP CLEARED 2026-08-09 (operator-authorised push, 13/13 names re-verified clean on the public remote); GIT HISTORY NOT YET PURGED.

17 traded names have no business record in companies.yaml, so they render as backlog-less on the order-book surface. Exposed when the Monday 10-Aug post-close run regenerated the aggregate; test_business_models.py went red. The test is CORRECT — do not relax it.
fib_radar / fib_confluences carry 2026-08-10 (and prev_close) prices under a declared 2026-08-11 session -- 21 rows across three blocks

Two of step 1's three price-cache repairs had no write-side guard, so the rolling 1-year re-fetch undid both within 16 hours. Guards now shipped and the data repaired; the residue on SILVER1 is an operator call.

The 23-Aug capital-gains report books six securities of NEW realised activity after the 13-Aug drop, including two names the held book has never carried and a delivery sell of exactly the CHAMBLFERT lot still shown as held. The book is no longer merely stale — it is demonstrably WRONG, and the capital-gains report is the only surface that can see it.

propagate_positions.py --push cannot complete its rebase whenever the repo clone holds vault-written copies of cron-owned files. Those copies accumulate silently from the morning scheduled run and were 5-6 hours OLDER than what the cloud cron had already published, so the obvious manual fix (git add -A) would have reverted the silver desk and the notifications feed.

21 names carry a hand-verified fib bank and no decision pass — no trim ladder, no invalidation level, no capital-freed number against them. Queued as one dedicated exercise; scope, chart spec, page template and workflow are in the vault-local plan doc. Blocked on four operator inputs.

fib_confluences.method: fib-box confluence = box edges from TWO+ different ladders within ~1.5% of each other
fib_confluences.note: Engine-detected cross-ladder fib-box confluences from verified banks (box_engine.py). Surfaced for operator validation over time — observations, not calls. Every px = a banked ladder's box edge; distance is vs the live price. AT = within ~2% of the confluence.

fib_level_quality.memory_note: arxiv 2101.07410: a level with more prior bounces is more likely to bounce again. If that holds here, share_nearer RISES with the bucket.
fib_level_quality.age_note: Bucketed on pivot_date - studied_date, so this measures LEVEL AGE rather than position in the sample. If levels decay, share_nearer FALLS with the bucket -- and the bank schema's EVERGREEN claim is wrong. NOTE the residual confound: the oldest banks are a different SET of names, not the same names grown older, so a name-mix effect cannot be fully separated in this window.
fib_level_quality.decay_note: arxiv 2101.07410 reports the bounce probability DECAYING over time. Our bank schema calls levels EVERGREEN, so a real decay here contradicts a standing assumption rather than merely adding a feature.

level_memory.basis: NSE bhavcopy daily OHLC; a touch is a bar whose range comes within 0.35 ATR of the level, and a return only counts as a NEW touch after 3 sessions away.
level_memory.window_note: The count window is part of the threshold. TESTED_AT was calibrated inside the study's ~32-session window; counting over a year would make almost every level 'tested'.

evidence.claim: A level price has already visited 2+ times catches a pivot 82.5% of the time, against 67.5% for one it has never returned to.
evidence.source: measured in fib_level_quality.py against a scrambled-ladder null; direction predicted first by arxiv 2101.07410
evidence.limit: Says a level is more likely to be WHERE price turns. Says nothing about WHEN or which way -- a touch still predicts nothing at 3/5/10 days.
